items.headline: Planning Commission agenda: 316 apartments at 400 Saratoga Avenue golf course
items.summary: The November 18 Planning Commission agenda listed a recommendation on amending the General Plan and rezoning 400 Saratoga Avenue for a five-story, 316-unit apartment building. The plan would also reconfigure the existing nine-hole golf course and dedicate land for a public park. An environmental impact report was prepared for the project.

items.headline: Townhomes and a duplex with commercial space proposed on Civic Center Drive
items.summary: The November 18 Planning Commission agenda listed a vesting tentative subdivision map for condominium purposes covering 14 townhomes and a duplex building with commercial space at 860 and 858 Civic Center Drive and 1526 Alviso Street. The item cited a CEQA exemption under AB 130 (2025).

items.headline: Appeal over Rita Court home addition on Planning Commission agenda
items.summary: The November 18 agenda listed an appeal of a staff-level architectural review approval at 2261 Rita Court. The approval covers a 517-square-foot first-floor addition and a 1,000-square-foot second-floor addition to a single-story home on a 6,272-square-foot lot.

items.headline: 69-stall surface parking lot proposed at 2740 Scott Boulevard
items.summary: The November 18 Planning Commission agenda listed a conditional use permit for a 69-stall surface parking lot at 2740 Scott Boulevard. It also listed architectural review for demolition of the existing vacant structures and a minor use permit for off-site parking.

items.headline: Two lawsuits listed for the Cupertino City Council's closed session
items.summary: The November 17 City Council agenda listed a closed-session conference with legal counsel on existing litigation: Lixin (Leon) Chen, et al. v. City of Cupertino, and Yes in My Backyard, et al. v. City of Cupertino. Both cases are in Santa Clara County Superior Court. The agenda does not describe the claims.

items.headline: Cupertino agenda included an ordinance on council compensation
items.summary: The November 17 City Council agenda listed an ordinance amending Cupertino Municipal Code Section 2.16.020, which covers council compensation. The same agenda listed subcommittee recommendations on the community funding policy and festival fee waivers.

items.headline: Campbell agenda listed a hearing on single-family rezoning at 480 Chapman
items.summary: The November 10 Planning Commission agenda listed a public hearing on a request by GKW Architects on behalf of owners Joseph and Alicia Lam to change 480 Chapman from Neighborhood Commercial to Low Density Residential (R-1-10 zoning). The existing house is a legal nonconforming use under the current commercial designation, and the change would end that status. Staff recommended that the commission urge the City Council to approve the change. The City Council could take it up on December 1, 2026.

items.headline: Cupertino commission agenda lists 251-unit Eden Housing project on N. Wolfe Road
items.summary: The November 10 Planning Commission agenda listed Architectural and Site Approval and Tree Removal Permits for Eden Housing's proposed 251-unit residential development at 10333 N. Wolfe Road. The request includes site and trail improvements and the removal and replacement of 117 protected trees.
